title: Europe’s Positive GDP Print Conceals a Slower Impulse
trigger: Eurostat’s 30 October flash estimate showed euro-area GDP growth easing from 0.6% q/q in Q2 to 0.4% in Q3, and EU growth easing from 0.7% to 0.5%.
limitations: GDP observations are preliminary quarter-on-quarter growth estimates and may be revised. The model applies a change in quarterly GDP growth to a hypothetical annual revenue reference base as a simplified sensitivity convention; the time horizons are not aligned. The revenue sensitivity multiplier is assumed rather than empirically estimated. The calculation does not identify causality, incorporate transmission lags, FX movements, sector composition or customer-specific demand, and must not be interpreted as a forecast or an estimate of actual revenue losses.
formula: Observed GDP-growth momentum (pp) = Q3 GDP growth (% q/q) − Q2 GDP growth (% q/q). Illustrative sensitivity indicator (€m) = annual exposed revenue reference base (€m) × assumed sensitivity multiplier × [observed GDP-growth momentum (pp) + additional momentum shock (pp)] / 100. The output is a hypothetical monetary sensitivity indicator, not a time-aligned annual revenue forecast or an empirically calibrated causal estimate.
decision: Use leading order-book indicators and customer concentration to test whether European growth deceleration affects the next two quarters of sales. Reconcile the time horizons and validate against company-specific demand and FX exposure before using the scenario for financial planning.
worked_example: Illustrative scenario: euro-area quarterly GDP growth decelerated by 0.2 percentage points. Applying this change mechanically to a hypothetical €1,000m annual exposed revenue reference base, with an assumed sensitivity multiplier of 1.5 and no additional shock, produces a −€3.0m sensitivity indicator. This is neither an observed revenue loss nor a projected annual revenue decline.
